Definition: from G1210; a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency):--bond(-man), servant.
BiblicalUsage: A bondservant, a slave, the word Jesus used when He said whoever would be first must be the servant of all, and when He washed the disciples' feet, saying the servant is not greater than his lord. Paul thanks God that the Romans, once servants of sin, obeyed the form of doctrine delivered to them, and that Christ took the form of a servant.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gospel turns slavery upside down: the Master became a servant, and His servants become sons. I am no longer a slave to sin but a servant of righteousness, and that service is the highest honour I know.
